q: What must you do when you face this traffic signal?
choices: Speed up to clear the intersection before it changes
Stop completely before the stop line or crosswalk
Slow down and go through if the way is clear
Proceed with caution after yielding to pedestrians
hint: Look at which colour is lit and whether it is steady or flashing.
explain: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the stop line or crosswalk and stay stopped until it turns green, unless you are safely turning right after stopping.
quote: Drivers facing a traffic control signal displaying a solid red light must bring their vehicles to a complete stop before the stop line or crosswalk that is directly in front of the vehicle.
topic: Steady red / green light basics

q: You want to turn right at this light and no sign prohibits the turn. What must you do first?
choices: Come to a complete stop before the stop line or crosswalk
Slow down and check for traffic, without stopping
Wait for the light to turn green
Move into the crosswalk so you can see better
hint: A right turn here is allowed, but only after one required step.
explain: Unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn right at a red light after a complete stop before the stop line or crosswalk, and only when it is safe after yielding to other traffic.
quote: Turning right at a red light is permitted provided that there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Before making the turn the vehicle must come to a complete stop before the stop line or crosswalk.
topic: Turning on a red light

q: You are approaching an intersection and this light comes on. What must you do?
choices: Speed up so you get through before it turns red
Stop, then go when the way is clear, as at a stop sign
Slow down and go through after yielding to pedestrians
Stop before the stop line or crosswalk, unless you can no longer stop safely
hint: This light warns that the signal is about to change to red.
explain: A steady yellow means the light will turn red right away. You must stop before the stop line or crosswalk unless you are too close to stop safely.
quote: Drivers approaching an intersection with a solid (not flashing) yellow traffic control light must bring their vehicles to a complete stop before the stop line or crosswalk, unless a point has been reached at the intersection where stopping cannot be done safely.
topic: Steady yellow light: stop if safe to do so

q: You face this light and want to turn left. What must you do?
choices: Stop completely first, then turn when it is safe
Wait, because left turns are not allowed on a solid green
Yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk
Turn without yielding, because oncoming traffic has a red light
hint: A steady green lets you go, but it does not put you ahead of everyone.
explain: A solid green lets you go through the intersection, but when turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
quote: Drivers facing a solid green traffic control light are permitted to travel through the intersection without stopping, unless required to yield to oncoming traffic when turning left or to pedestrians in the crosswalk when turning right or left.
topic: Steady red / green light basics

q: What does this signal allow you to do?
choices: Prepare to stop, because the light is about to turn red
Go in the direction of the arrow without yielding
Go in the direction of the arrow only after stopping
Go only in the direction of the arrow and nowhere else
hint: Notice that both the arrow and the round green light are lit.
explain: With a green arrow and a green light, you may go in the arrow's direction without yielding. You may also go in other directions when it is safe and legal.
quote: Drivers facing a traffic control light with a green arrow and solid green traffic control light may enter the intersection and proceed without yielding in the direction indicated by the arrow.
topic: Green/yellow turn arrows (protected vs permissive turns)

q: What may you do when you face this signal?
choices: Go without stopping, but only in the direction of the arrow
Go in any direction, because the arrow cancels the red light
Stay stopped until the round light turns green
Stop first, then go in any direction when it is safe
hint: The red light still applies to every movement the arrow does not show.
explain: With a green arrow and a red light, you may enter the intersection without stopping, but only in the direction the arrow points.
quote: Drivers facing a traffic control light with a green arrow and a red control light may enter the intersection and proceed without stopping only in the direction indicated by the arrow.
topic: Green/yellow turn arrows (protected vs permissive turns)

q: What does this flashing light mean?
choices: Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping
Oncoming traffic has a red light, so you may go
The light is about to turn green, so get ready
Treat it like a stop sign
hint: Compare it with a flashing yellow light; this colour asks for more.
explain: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. Stop before the stop line or crosswalk, and go only when it is safe after yielding.
quote: The flashing red light is treated like a stop sign.
topic: Flashing red light = treat as stop sign

q: What does this flashing light tell you?
choices: The light is about to turn red, so speed up
Oncoming traffic has a red light, so you may turn freely
You may proceed with caution after yielding to pedestrians and other vehicles
You must come to a complete stop, as at a stop sign
hint: Compare it with a flashing red; this colour asks for less.
explain: A flashing yellow light lets you proceed with caution after yielding to pedestrians and other vehicles within the intersection.
quote: Drivers facing a flashing yellow traffic control light may proceed with caution after yielding to pedestrians and other vehicles within the intersection.
topic: Flashing yellow/amber light = slow, proceed with caution

q: You face this flashing green light and want to turn left. What is true?
choices: Left turns are not allowed until the light stops flashing
Oncoming traffic faces a red light, so you may turn without stopping
Oncoming traffic also has a green light, so wait for a gap
You must stop first, then turn when the way is clear
hint: Think about what the drivers coming toward you are facing.
explain: A flashing green lets you go through, turn left or turn right without stopping because opposing traffic faces a red light. You must still yield to pedestrians or vehicles lawfully in the intersection.
quote: Drivers facing a flashing green traffic control light are permitted to go through, turn left or turn right without stopping. Opposing traffic will be facing a red light; however a driver must still yield to pedestrians or other vehicles lawfully in the intersection.
topic: Flashing green / advance green: protected turn

q: What does this sign mark?
choices: A pedestrian crossing
A road where pedestrians are not permitted
A school area where children may be walking
A playground zone with a 30 km/h limit
hint: There is no red circle on this sign, so nothing is being prohibited.
explain: This white sign with a walking person and a line under the feet is a pedestrian crossing sign.
quote: Pedestrian crossing signs without yellow lights.
topic: Pedestrian crosswalk / pedestrian-related signs

q: This signal is shown over a driving lane. What does it mean?
choices: The lane is closed only to trucks and buses
You may use the lane, but only to pass
A railway crossing is ahead in that lane
Do not enter or stay in that lane; oncoming traffic is using it
hint: These signals are used on lanes that change direction at different times of day.
explain: A red X over a lane means do not enter or remain in that lane, because oncoming traffic is using it. Move safely into a lane with a green arrow.
quote: When a red X is displayed over a driving lane, the driver does not enter or remain in that lane. This signal indicates that the lane is being used by oncoming traffic.
topic: Lane control signals (red X, green arrow) / reversible lanes

q: What does this signal over a lane tell you?
choices: You must turn at the next intersection
The lane is reserved for buses and taxis
You are permitted to travel in that lane
The lane ends ahead, so merge left
hint: Lane reversal signals switch between a red X and this symbol.
explain: A downward pointing green arrow over a lane means you are permitted to travel in that lane.
quote: A driver facing the downward pointing green arrow is permitted to travel in that lane.
topic: Lane control signals (red X, green arrow) / reversible lanes

q: What does a sign with this shape and fluorescent yellow-green colour indicate?
choices: A hazard such as a curve or hill
A school zone or school area
A construction area
A place for food, fuel, or lodging
hint: This five-sided shape is used for only one kind of place.
explain: A fluorescent yellow-green, pentagon-shaped sign indicates a school zone or school area.
quote: Indicates school zone/area. Fluorescent yellow green background Pentagon shape
topic: Sign shapes/colours meanings

q: What type of sign is a yellow diamond like this one?
choices: A warning of a hazard shown on the sign
A regulatory sign, such as a speed limit
A sign giving construction area information
A guide sign showing distance to a destination
hint: Think about the colour and the shape together.
explain: Yellow diamond signs give caution or warning of the hazard shown on the sign. This one warns of a bump.
quote: Indicates caution or warning of hazard displayed on sign. Information or pictures on yellow background Diamond shape
topic: Sign shapes/colours meanings

q: What does the orange colour of this diamond sign tell you?
choices: It warns of a school zone ahead
It shows a place for fuel, food, or lodging
It marks a route for dangerous goods
It gives construction area information
hint: Compare it with the yellow diamond signs; only the colour is different.
explain: Orange diamond signs give construction area information. This one warns of a survey crew ahead.
quote: Provides construction area information. Information or picture on orange background Diamond shape
topic: Construction/temporary (orange) signs

q: What does a blue sign like this one show?
choices: The distance to a destination
A lane reserved for certain vehicles
A place for fuel, food, lodging, or assistance
A warning of a hazard ahead
hint: Look at the pictures inside the square.
explain: White symbols on a blue square show a place for fuel, food, lodging, or assistance. This one shows food.
quote: Indicates place for fuel, food, lodging, or assistance. White message on blue background Square shape
topic: Information/guide/service signs

q: What kind of information does a green rectangular sign like this give?
choices: Construction area information
Information such as the distance to a destination
A warning of a hazard on the road ahead
A regulatory message such as a speed limit
hint: Think about the colour and the shape together.
explain: White messages on a green rectangle give information such as the distance to a destination.
quote: Provides information such as distance to destination. White message on green background Rectangle shape
topic: Information/guide/service signs

q: What must you do at this sign?
choices: Come to a complete stop and go only when it is safe
Slow down and go through without stopping if the way is clear
Stop only if other vehicles are coming
Slow to 30 km/h and watch for children
hint: Think about whether slowing down is ever enough at this sign.
explain: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop and not proceed until it is safe.
quote: Stop: Come to a complete stop and do not proceed until safe.
topic: Stop / yield / stop-ahead / yield-ahead signs

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: You have the right-of-way over cross traffic
Traffic ahead is moving toward you in your lane
Stop at the line every time, even if the road is clear
Let traffic not facing the sign, and pedestrians, go first
hint: This sign tells you who goes first, and it is not you.
explain: A yield sign means you must give the right-of-way to traffic not facing the sign and to pedestrians waiting to cross or already in the crosswalk or intersection.
quote: Yield the right-of-way to traffic not facing the sign and to all pedestrians waiting to cross and within the crosswalk or intersection.
topic: Yield sign: slow/stop as needed, yield to traffic and pedestrians

q: You see this sign facing you. What does it tell you?
choices: Two-way traffic begins ahead
A divider is ahead, so keep to the right
Traffic is moving toward you in the oncoming direction
The road ahead is one-way in your direction
hint: Think about which way you are travelling compared with the other traffic.
explain: The guide says this sign indicates that traffic is moving in an oncoming direction.
quote: Wrong way: Indicates traffic is moving in an oncoming direction.
topic: Prohibitive signs (do not enter, wrong way)

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: No U-turn
Do not enter
No parking
No stopping
hint: This red circle has a white bar instead of a picture.
explain: The red circle with a white horizontal bar is the Do not enter sign.
quote: Do not enter:
topic: Prohibitive signs (no left/right/U-turn, do not enter)

q: What does this sign tell you?
choices: Do not stop on the railway tracks
Stop before the tracks every time
Railway crossing ahead, so reduce speed
No stopping on the days and times shown
hint: Look at what is drawn under the red circle.
explain: The crossed-out stop symbol above a picture of railway tracks means do not stop on tracks.
quote: Do not stop on tracks:
topic: Railway crossing signs

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Turn right only at the next intersection
Two-way traffic is ahead
Keep right of a divider ahead
Proceed only in the direction of the arrow
hint: The words and the arrow work together.
explain: This traffic direction sign means proceed in the direction of the arrow only.
quote: Proceed in direction of arrow only:
topic: Lane-use / turn-control signs (one way)

q: What does this sign tell you about the road?
choices: The left lane ends ahead
A divided highway begins
Traffic travels in both directions
Traffic travels in one direction only
hint: Look at which way each arrow points.
explain: This traffic direction sign means two-way traffic.
quote: Two way traffic:
topic: Divided highway, keep right, two-way traffic

q: What should you do when you see this sign?
choices: Pass on the left of the island ahead
Keep to the right of the divider ahead
Merge left because your lane is ending
Turn right at the next intersection
hint: The rounded black shape stands for something in the middle of the road.
explain: This sign means a divider is ahead and you must keep right.
quote: Divider ahead – keep right:
topic: Divided highway, keep right, two-way traffic

q: This route marker shows you are on a provincial highway. Unless another limit is posted, what is the maximum speed outside an urban area?
choices: 100 km/h
80 km/h
60 km/h
50 km/h
hint: Think about the default limit for highways that run between communities.
explain: Unless otherwise posted, 100 km/h is the maximum speed limit on a provincial highway outside an urban area. Inside a city's corporate limits it is 80 km/h.
quote: 100 km/h is the maximum speed limit on a provincial highway located outside an urban area.
topic: Speed limit signs

q: Which movements may you make from a lane with this sign over it?
choices: Turn right only
Go straight or turn left
Turn left or turn right only
Go straight or turn right
hint: Follow each arrow from its base.
explain: Designated lane signs show the direction(s) you must travel in that lane. This one allows going straight or turning right.
quote: The message or symbol on these signs indicates the direction(s) a vehicle must travel in the lane.
topic: Lane-use / turn-control signs

q: This sign shows that two lanes may turn left at the same time. What should you do while turning?
choices: Let the other turning lane go first, then turn
Change lanes in the middle of the turn if it is clear
Stay in your own lane during and after the turn
Move to the right lane as soon as the turn is done
hint: Picture the car turning beside you the whole way through.
explain: Where more than one lane may turn at the same time, keep your lane position during and after the turn.
quote: Some intersections allow more than one vehicle travelling in the same direction to turn at the same time. Maintain your lane position during and after the turn.
topic: Dual/double turn lanes

q: What does this sign over a lane mean?
choices: The lane is a two-way left turn lane at the times shown
The lane is reserved for buses and taxis at the times shown
Buses and taxis may not use the lane at the times shown
Parking is allowed in the lane at the times shown
hint: The diamond and the pictures tell you who the lane is for.
explain: Reserved lane signs use symbols to show which vehicles may use the lane. Lanes reserved only part of the time show the hours and days.
quote: Indicated lanes are reserved for specific vehicles such as buses, taxis, and bicycles. The symbol on the sign will identify the vehicles permitted to travel in this lane.
topic: Reserved lanes (HOV diamond, bus, bicycle lanes)

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: You may only turn left
Left turns are not allowed
A sharp turn to the left is ahead
The left lane ends ahead
hint: Green circles and red circles mean opposite things.
explain: A green circle means the action inside is permitted. This sign means turn left only.
quote: Permission signs are a green circle on a white square. The action within the green circle is permitted. Turn left only:
topic: Lane-use / turn-control signs

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Passing is not permitted
Two-way traffic is ahead
A divided highway begins
Passing is permitted
hint: Check the colour of the circle.
explain: A green circle means the action shown is permitted, so this sign means passing is permitted.
quote: Permission signs are a green circle on a white square. The action within the green circle is permitted. ... Passing permitted:
topic: Passing permitted / do not pass signs

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: A sharp turn to the left ahead
No U-turn
No left turn
Left turn only
hint: Think about what a red slash does to the picture under it.
explain: The red circle and slash mean the action shown is not permitted. This sign means no left turn.
quote: The action within the red circle is not permitted. No left turn:
topic: Prohibitive signs (no left/right/U-turn, do not enter)

q: What does the red circle and slash on this sign tell you?
choices: The action shown is a hazard ahead
The action shown inside the circle is not permitted
The action shown inside the circle is permitted
The action shown is allowed only at certain times
hint: Compare it with signs that use a green circle.
explain: A red circle with a diagonal red bar on a white square means the action within the circle is not permitted. This sign means no right turn.
quote: The symbol prohibiting an action is a red circle and diagonal red bar on a white square. The action within the red circle is not permitted.
topic: Prohibitive signs (no left/right/U-turn, do not enter)

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Do not pass
Passing permitted
Do not pass bicycles
Two-way traffic ahead
hint: Check the colour of the circle and what is inside it.
explain: A red circle and slash over two cars means do not pass.
quote: The action within the red circle is not permitted. ... Do not pass:
topic: Passing permitted / do not pass signs

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Do not pass any vehicle
Bicycles are not permitted
Bicycle crossing ahead
Do not pass bicycles
hint: Look closely at what the car is beside.
explain: This prohibitive sign shows a car beside a cyclist inside a red circle and slash: do not pass bicycles.
quote: Do not pass bicycles:
topic: Passing permitted / do not pass signs

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Pedestrians are permitted to cross here
School crosswalk ahead
Pedestrians are not permitted
Pedestrian crossing ahead
hint: Think about what a red slash does to the picture under it.
explain: The red circle and slash mean the action shown is not permitted, so pedestrians are not permitted.
quote: The symbol prohibiting an action is a red circle and diagonal red bar on a white square. The action within the red circle is not permitted.
topic: Prohibitive signs

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Dangerous goods are not permitted
Trucks are not permitted
Trucks are permitted
Trucks entering from the right ahead
hint: Check the colour of the circle and the picture inside it.
explain: A truck inside a red circle and slash means no trucks.
quote: No trucks:
topic: Prohibitive signs (no trucks/bicycles)

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Vehicles carrying dangerous goods are not permitted
Vehicles carrying dangerous goods are permitted
The lane is reserved for buses and taxis
Hazard marker: an object is on the right
hint: The black diamond inside a circle stands for a certain kind of cargo.
explain: The diamond symbol inside a red circle and slash means no dangerous goods.
quote: No dangerous goods:
topic: Reserved lanes, dangerous goods route

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Parking is allowed only in the direction of the arrow
No stopping in the direction the arrow points
Turn right to find parking
No parking in the direction the arrow points
hint: The letter in the circle tells you which action is limited, and the arrow tells you where.
explain: The P in a red circle and slash means no parking. The arrow under the symbol shows where parking is not permitted.
quote: The arrow under the symbol indicates where the action indicated on the sign is not permitted.
topic: Parking / no parking / no stopping signs

q: What does this sign mean?
choices: Stop sign ahead in both directions
Do not stop on the railway tracks
No stopping on either side of the sign
No stopping to the right of the sign only
hint: Look at the shape inside the red circle, then at the arrows.
explain: A stop-sign shape inside a red circle and slash means no stopping. The arrows show it applies on both sides of the sign.
quote: Parking and stopping not permitted: The arrow under the symbol indicates where the action indicated on the sign is not permitted.
topic: Parking / no parking / no stopping signs

q: When are you not allowed to park near this sign?
choices: Any time outside 9:00 to 16:00, Monday to Friday
From 9:00 to 16:00, Monday to Friday
At all times, every day of the week
From 9:00 to 16:00 on weekends only
hint: Read the times and days printed under the symbol.
explain: This sign means no parking on the days and times shown: 9:00 to 16:00, Monday to Friday.
quote: No parking on the days and times shown:
topic: Parking / no parking / no stopping signs

q: This school sign has a maximum speed sign posted with it. Unless other times are posted, when is the school zone in effect?
choices: School days only: 8:00 to 9:30 a.m., 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., and 3:00 to 4:30 p.m.
Every day from 8:30 a.m. to one hour after sunset
School days only, from 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. without a break
Every day of the week, at all hours of the day and night
hint: School zones and playground zones run on different schedules.
explain: Unless a municipality posts different times, school zones are in effect on school days only, from 8:00 to 9:30 a.m., 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., and 3:00 to 4:30 p.m.
quote: The times that the school zone is in effect are on school days only and are as follows: 8:00 a.m. – 9:30 a.m. 11:30 a.m. – 1:30 p.m. 3:00 p.m. – 4:30 p.m.
topic: School zone: 30 km/h and default hours on school days

q: This school sign has no speed sign attached to it. What does it mean?
choices: A school zone: do not exceed 30 km/h while it is in effect
A playground area: children may be playing nearby
The end of a school zone: return to the posted speed
A school area: use caution, children may be walking or crossing
hint: Whether a speed sign is attached decides between a zone and an area.
explain: A school sign without a speed sign marks a school area. It alerts you that children may be walking or crossing the road, so use caution.
quote: When you approach a school sign without a speed sign attached to it, you are entering a school area. This sign is to alert drivers that children may be walking or crossing the road and you must use caution when driving through the school area.
topic: School zone / school crosswalk signs

q: You are driving through a school zone and pass this sign. What does it mean?
choices: A playground zone begins here
You may pass, but the school zone continues
The school zone has ended
The school zone limit is now 50 km/h
hint: Compare this number with the school zone speed limit.
explain: A school zone ends where a sign shows a higher maximum speed or the end of the school zone.
quote: A school zone ends where a traffic sign indicates: 1. a higher maximum speed, or 2. the end of the school zone.
topic: School zone

q: What does this sign alert you to do?
choices: Keep off the road, which is for pedestrians only
Watch for pedestrians at a school crosswalk
Slow to 30 km/h every day until one hour after sunset
Get ready to stop for a school bus ahead
hint: Notice the line under the children's feet.
explain: This is the school crosswalk sign. It alerts drivers to watch for pedestrians.
quote: School crosswalk: This sign alerts drivers to watch for pedestrians.
topic: School zone / school crosswalk signs

q: This playground sign has a maximum speed sign attached. Unless other times are posted, when is the playground zone in effect?
choices: Every day from 8:30 a.m. to one hour after sunset
School days only, from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
Weekdays only, from 8:30 a.m. to sunset
Every day from 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
hint: Playgrounds are used on weekends and in the evening too.
explain: Playground zone restrictions are in effect every day from 8:30 a.m. to one hour after sunset, unless the municipality posts different times.
quote: Playground restrictions are in effect every day from 8:30 a.m. to one hour after sunset.
topic: Playground zone: 30 km/h, 8:30 a.m. to 1 hr after sunset, every day

q: This playground sign has no speed limit sign attached. What does it tell you?
choices: Do not exceed 30 km/h from 8:30 a.m. to one hour after sunset
A school zone is in effect on school days
Pedestrians are not permitted on the road
Children may be near, so use caution
hint: Without a speed sign, this is an area rather than a zone.
explain: A playground sign without a speed limit sign marks a playground area. Children may be near, so use caution.
quote: When you approach a playground sign without a speed limit sign attached to it, you are entering a playground area. This sign is to alert drivers that children may be near and you must use caution when driving through the playground area.
topic: Playground zone / playground ahead signs

q: Which vehicles may park or stop in a stall marked with this sign?
choices: Any vehicle, for up to 15 minutes
Any vehicle picking up or dropping off a passenger
Only vehicles with a disability parking placard or licence plate
Any vehicle, if the driver stays inside
hint: Being there only briefly does not change the rule.
explain: It is illegal for any vehicle to park or stop in a stall reserved for persons with disabilities unless it has an identifying parking placard or licence plate.
quote: It is illegal for any vehicle to park or stop in a parking stall reserved for persons with disabilities unless the vehicle has an identifying parking placard or licence plate.
topic: Parking / disabled parking signs

q: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: A railway crossing is ahead
A stop sign is ahead
A yield sign is ahead
Traffic control signals are ahead
hint: Look at the shape and colour of the symbol under the arrow.
explain: This yellow warning sign gives advance notice of a stop sign ahead.
quote: Traffic regulations: Stop ahead
topic: Stop / yield / stop-ahead / yield-ahead signs

q: What does this yellow sign warn you about?
choices: A yield sign is ahead
A stop sign is ahead
Merging traffic is ahead
A school bus stop is ahead
hint: Look at the shape of the symbol under the arrow.
explain: This yellow warning sign gives advance notice of a yield sign ahead.
quote: Yield ahead
topic: Stop / yield / stop-ahead / yield-ahead signs

q: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: A railway crossing with lights is ahead
A stop sign is ahead
A pedestrian crossing is ahead
Traffic control signals are ahead
hint: Count the lights and look at their colours.
explain: This warning sign means traffic control signals are ahead.
quote: Traffic control signals ahead
topic: Intersection-ahead warnings

q: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: A bus lane begins ahead
A school crosswalk is ahead
A school bus stop is ahead
A school zone begins ahead
hint: Look at the vehicle in the picture and who is beside it.
explain: This warning sign means a school bus stop is ahead.
quote: School bus stop ahead
topic: School zone / school bus stop ahead signs

q: The yellow lights on this sign are flashing. What should you do?
choices: Stop beside the sign until the lights stop flashing
Prepare to stop, because the signal ahead is changing to red or is red
Speed up to get through the green light ahead
Slow to 30 km/h for a school zone
hint: The sign shows what the traffic light ahead is about to do.
explain: This sign is placed before some signalized intersections. When its yellow lights flash, the signal ahead is turning from green to yellow or yellow to red, or is already red, so prepare to stop.
quote: When the yellow lights are flashing, drivers approaching the intersection must prepare to stop because the traffic control signal light will be turning from green to yellow or yellow to red, or is currently red.
topic: Intersection-ahead warnings

q: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: A sharp turn to the right
A right turn only lane
A hidden road joining from the right
A winding road ahead
hint: Look at the angle in the arrow.
explain: This yellow warning sign means a sharp turn to the right is ahead.
quote: Sharp turn right
topic: Curve, sharp turn, winding road, chevron, advisory-speed signs

q: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: The road is slippery when wet
Merging traffic ahead
A divided highway begins
A winding road ahead
hint: Count how many times the arrow bends.
explain: This yellow warning sign means a winding road is ahead.
quote: Winding road
topic: Curve, sharp turn, winding road, chevron, advisory-speed signs

q: This yellow sign is posted below a curve warning sign. What does the number mean?
choices: The speed limit for the rest of the highway
The speed at which speeding fines are doubled
The recommended maximum speed through the curve in ideal conditions
The legal minimum speed on the curve
hint: This number goes with the curve sign above it.
explain: The yellow speed sign under a curve sign is the recommended maximum speed through that curve under ideal driving conditions.
quote: Recommended maximum speed through this curve under ideal driving conditions
topic: Curve, sharp turn, winding road, chevron, advisory-speed signs

q: What does this yellow diamond sign warn you about?
choices: A playground area ahead
A pedestrian crossing ahead
Pedestrians are not permitted ahead
A bicycle crossing ahead
hint: Look at the person and the line under their feet.
explain: This yellow warning sign means a pedestrian crossing is ahead.
quote: Crossings ahead: Pedestrian crossing
topic: Pedestrian crosswalk / pedestrian-related signs

q: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: Moose may be crossing ahead
Falling rock ahead
Motorized snow vehicles crossing ahead
A trailer campground ahead
hint: Look at the animal in the picture.
explain: This yellow warning sign means a moose crossing is ahead.

topic: Railway crossing signs (crossbuck, advance warning, X marking)

topic: Railway crossing signs (crossbuck, advance warning, X marking)
